Driver survey 2026-11-08: Python and TypeScript/Node about 65 to 75 percent combined. Absorbs card 108 (open, Ready, specs only). Narrows card 028 (open, Ready, TypeScript seed-catalogue spike).

- **Story:** As Dana, I want one tiny program to produce passing specs in Python or TypeScript, so that I can keep my stack.
- **Consumer value:** Dana keeps a Python or TypeScript stack; we see it when the same leaf, failure and spec build for that target and the specs pass.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Scenario: [O][S] one tiny program, specs pass
     Given Dana's stack named in this Given as Python or TypeScript, and the same leaf, failure and spec
     When built for that target
     Then the specs pass
  2. Scenario: [I] same specs become tests in that language
     Given those specs
     When compiled to tests in that language (card 108, specs only, absorbed)
     Then there is one test per spec with the same inputs and expected outcomes, and the compiler core references no adapter (card 040)
  3. Scenario: [E] a mutation fails a spec
     Given a one-line mutation of that implementation
     When the generated tests run
     Then at least one fails
  Letters that do not apply: [Z] a missing-adapter diagnostic is card 347 and 028's Zero; [M] the seed catalogue is 028, narrowed to one program; [B] language-level differences (null, integer width) are 028's Boundaries.
- **Not in this card:** card 345 Wasm; card 347 plugin command; card 348; card 349; publishing; a registry; a language server; a UI; the rest of 028 (eight-plus seed keywords on TypeScript).
- **Unknowns:** which of Python or TypeScript this Given names (card 108 left that to a Decider note); how far the C#-shaped map records must change for this target. A spike is allowed only once card 346 is the top story.
